title: Leeds City Council and Xylo: transforming planning with AI
summary: Leeds reports over 40% more applications processed per officer, less research time, and improved officer wellbeing during its Xylo pilot.
account: Leeds co-designed and piloted Xylo Core to support planning officers from post-validation through determination. Officer interviews and usage data reportedly show over 40% more householder/minor applications processed monthly per officer, with reduced research and consultation-processing time. Percentages come from project-side interviews and usage data. The page does not provide sample sizes or an independent causal evaluation.
purpose: Help planning officers find and process relevant information while retaining professional judgment.

ratings.reason: Reported application throughput rises by over 40%, supporting a measurable service-capability gain.

All surveyed officers reportedly experienced improved stress and energy levels, alongside less research work. These are reported wellbeing/work-capability improvements without a demonstrated lasting change.

ai_role.statement: The workspace brings together planning-application content and context to support research and processing tasks. The reported throughput and wellbeing figures come from officer interviews and usage data, without an independent causal comparison.

evidence.citation: Local Government Association, AI case-study bank. Council or project account published by LGA. Hosting and editorial curation do not establish independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Leeds City Council and Xylo: transforming planning with AI

produced_by: Leeds and Xylo co-designed and tested the workspace over more than six months.
The reported pilot focused on time, work quality, and officer wellbeing.
must_hold: The source does not establish which conditions are necessary to reproduce the reported benefit.

headline: Leeds reports more planning applications processed with Xylo
